claims.statement: One row represents a single robot record (the base entity for a robot instance).
One row represents the detail/profile snapshot for one robot, in a strict 1:1 relationship with robot_record.
One row represents a single operation instance for a robot, in a 1:1 relationship with robot_record and robot_details.
One row represents a single actuation reading, which is in a strict 1:1 relationship with one operation and one robot record rather than one of many time-stamped readings per operation.
One row represents the maintenance/fault assessment tied to one actuation (and hence one operation and one robot).
One row represents the performance/safety measurement tied to one actuation.
One row represents the controller metrics record tied to one actuation.

Although no primary key is declared, jcdetref (and likewise jcondoperref, jcrecref) is unique per row, so one row represents the joint-condition snapshot tied to exactly one robot, one operation and one record; the 1:1 grain is enforced only by the data, not by a schema constraint.

Although no primary key is declared, jperfdetref is unique per row, so one row represents the joint-performance snapshot tied to exactly one robot, one operation and one record, with the 1:1 grain enforced only by the data.

Although no primary key is declared, mechdetref is unique per row, so one row represents the mechanical-status snapshot tied to exactly one robot, one operation and one record, with the 1:1 grain enforced only by the data.

progcyclecount happens to be unique across all 1,000 rows; this is likely a coincidence of the data rather than evidence that program-cycle counts are designed to be unique identifiers, so it should not be relied on as a key.
upkeepcostest happens to be unique across all 1,000 rows; this is likely a coincidence of continuous-valued cost estimates rather than a meaningful key.

The dataset is structured so that every robot record has exactly one matching robot_details, operation, and actuation_data row (and downstream tables), i.e. it is a one-reading-per-robot snapshot extract rather than a time series of multiple operations or readings per robot.

Installation dates recorded for robots span 2022-05-27 to 2024-11-11 (31 distinct months); robots installed outside this window, if any exist in reality, are not present in this extract, and any time trend ending at 2024-11-11 reflects the extract cutoff, not necessarily a real-world decline.

Every actuation has a matching maintenance_and_fault row, but a large share of them carry no fault code, issue category, issue level, or fault-type estimation, meaning most actuations in this extract show no detected fault or issue rather than missing records.
A 'fault' is identified by a non-empty faultcodeval; the ~48.7% of rows where it is empty are actuations with no fault recorded, not missing data to be imputed.
Empty/null values mean no fault code was raised for that actuation rather than an unrecorded measurement.
Holds a categorical fault/issue category (Mechanical, Electrical, Communication, Software) with null meaning no issue category applies to that actuation (about 20% of rows).
Holds an ordinal-looking severity scale (Low, Medium, High, Critical) with null meaning no active issue/severity applies (about 18% of rows).
Holds a categorical estimated fault origin (Gearbox, Motor, Controller, Joint) with null meaning no fault type was estimated for that actuation (about 21.6% of rows).
Holds a three-level categorical status (Normal, Warning, Error) describing brake 1 condition, roughly evenly distributed, not a numeric severity.
Holds a three-level categorical status (Normal, Warning, Error) describing brake 2 condition.
Holds a three-level categorical status (Normal, Warning, Error) describing brake 3 condition.
Holds a three-level categorical status (Normal, Warning, Error) describing brake 4 condition.
Holds a three-level categorical status (Normal, Warning, Error) describing brake 5 condition.
Holds a three-level categorical status (Normal, Warning, Error) describing brake 6 condition.
Holds a three-level categorical status (Normal, Warning, Error) describing encoder 1 condition.
Holds a three-level categorical status (Normal, Warning, Error) describing encoder 2 condition.
Holds a three-level categorical status (Normal, Warning, Error) describing encoder 3 condition.
Holds a three-level categorical status (Normal, Warning, Error) describing encoder 4 condition.
Holds a three-level categorical status (Normal, Warning, Error) describing encoder 5 condition.
Holds a three-level categorical status (Normal, Warning, Error) describing encoder 6 condition.

Holds a fixed set of 5 robot application-type categories (Material Handling, Painting, Assembly, Palletizing, Welding); the 'word' vs 'phrase' format split flagged by automated checks is simply because some category names contain a space and is not a mix of different kinds of identifiers.

Holds a fixed set of 5 robot manufacturer names (FANUC, Universal Robots, Yaskawa, KUKA, ABB); the 'word' vs 'phrase' split flagged by checks is only because 'Universal Robots' contains a space, not a true mix of identifier types.
Holds a categorical controller-type code of the form Controller_<family><number> (15 distinct values across families A, B, C), identifying the controller model/series, not a free-text description.

Holds a continuous signed real-valued TCP x-position measurement; the numeric/alphanumeric split reported by automated checks is only an artifact of the minus sign on negative readings, not evidence of two different kinds of values.
Holds a continuous signed real-valued TCP y-position measurement; the numeric/alphanumeric split reported by automated checks is only an artifact of the minus sign on negative readings.

Holds a continuous signed real-valued TCP rotation (x-axis orientation) measurement; the numeric/alphanumeric split reported by automated checks is only an artifact of the minus sign on negative readings.

Holds a continuous signed real-valued TCP rotation (y-axis orientation) measurement; the numeric/alphanumeric split reported by automated checks is only an artifact of the minus sign on negative readings.

Holds a continuous signed real-valued TCP rotation (z-axis orientation) measurement; the numeric/alphanumeric split reported by automated checks is only an artifact of the minus sign on negative readings.

Stores a JSON-encoded object embedding multiple controller sub-metrics (e.g. a load_value field) as a single text value rather than one atomic measurement; grouping on the raw text therefore splits logically related readings into many near-duplicate categories because other embedded fields differ.

Stores a JSON-encoded object embedding multiple per-joint sub-metrics (e.g. joint1.angle) as a single text value rather than one atomic measurement, so each row's value is a composite record, not a simple scalar.
Stores a JSON-encoded object including an 'overloads' count (and likely other safety sub-metrics) as a single text value rather than one atomic measurement.

Operation application types and modes observed in this extract are limited to the 5 apptypeval categories found (Material Handling, Painting, Assembly, Palletizing, Welding); any other application type does not appear in this data.
Manufacturers represented in this extract are limited to the 5 found (FANUC, Universal Robots, Yaskawa, KUKA, ABB); other manufacturers are not covered by this data.
